findings.title: website_name is not listed in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors
findings.body: `:website` is included in `untrusted_attributes` (line 105-111) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous viewers (anti-spam/SEO measure). The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always serialized and now exposes the host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous requests. The front-end template renders `model.website_name` unconditionally, so the previously suppressed information becomes visible again. `:website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and the TL0 spec list updated).

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so the inclusion guard is dead code
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always emitted — including as `null` for every user without a website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that its body should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, see the untrusted-attributes issue).

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today only because literals are unfrozen; under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or if the file is ever frozen-string-literal enabled) this raises `FrozenError` at runtime for every profile serialization. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain comparison yields false positives on shared public suffixes
findings.body: The branch that strips the first label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares only the remaining labels, so unrelated sites that merely share a public suffix of the same label count are treated as the same domain — e.g. instance `forum.github.io` and user website `someone.github.io`, or any pair under a 3-label suffix. The result is that the full URL path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text. Consider restricting this to a registrable-domain comparison (e.g. PublicSuffix) or at least matching only when one host is a suffix of the other.

findings.title: Only URI path is appended; query/fragment are dropped and host matching is case sensitive
findings.body: `website_name` builds the display text from `host + path`, so for `http://example.com/u?tab=1#x` on a same-domain instance it renders `example.com/u`, silently hiding the part of the URL the feature is meant to disclose. Additionally `URI#host` preserves the case as typed, so `http://Example.com` never equals `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and falls into the generic branch. Downcase the host before comparing and include query/fragment (or use `URI#request_uri`) if the goal is to show the complete URL.

findings.title: TL0/anonymous spec does not assert website_name is withheld
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context was not updated with `website_name`, so the new attribute's exposure to anonymous viewers is untested and the regression described above passes CI. Add `website_name` to that list (after fixing the serializer) so the privacy guard is covered.

findings.title: Missing cases for sibling-subdomain branch and blank/invalid website
findings.body: The new specs cover only equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and website-domain-is-parent-of-instance. There is no coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch the code explicitly implements (e.g. instance `forum.example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/user`), for the reverse case (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), or for a blank/unparseable website (which must return nil without raising and ideally omit the key). These are the branches most likely to break.
